record.paper_title: On two long standing open problems on Lp-spaces
record.original_question: For a quasi-Banach Lebesgue space Lp with 0 < p < 1, is every complemented subspace of Lp isomorphic to Lp itself?

evidence.quote: Consider now the quasi-Banach spaces Lp for 0 < p < 1.
Problem 4. Let 0 <= p < 1. Is every complemented subspace of Lp isomorphic to Lp?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $0<p<1$ and consider the quasi-Banach space $L_p=L_p([0,1],\mathcal{B},\lambda)$, consisting of (equivalence classes of) measurable functions $f:[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}$ with $\|f\|_p:=\big(\int_0^1 |f(t)|^p\,dt\big)^{1/p}<\infty$, equipped with the quasi-norm $\|\cdot\|_p$ (which satisfies $\|f+g\|_p\le 2^{1/p-1}(\|f\|_p+\|g\|_p)$). A closed subspace $X\subseteq L_p$ is called complemented if there exists a continuous linear projection $P:L_p\to L_p$ with range $X$. Two quasi-Banach spaces are isomorphic if there exists a bijective continuous linear map between them whose inverse is also continuous.

Question: Is every infinite-dimensional complemented subspace of $L_p$ isomorphic to $L_p$ itself?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of classifying complemented subspaces of the non-locally convex quasi-Banach space $L_p$ for $0<p<1$ is a long-standing open problem. While the analogous question for $\ell_p$ ($0<p<1$) was solved by Stiles (every infinite-dimensional complemented subspace of $\ell_p$ is isomorphic to $\ell_p$), the corresponding question for $L_p$ with $0<p<1$ remains open, as discussed in Kalton's work and surveys on quasi-Banach spaces.

status_evidence.title: A Survey on the Complemented Subspace Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Considers complemented subspaces of Lp including the non-locally convex case.
status_evidence.claim: The structure of complemented subspaces of L_p for 0<p<1 is a classical and open area.

status_evidence.title: Kalton and Quasi-Banach Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Lebesgue spaces Lp are quasi-Banach for 0<p<1; structure problems remain open.
status_evidence.claim: Complemented subspace classification in L_p for 0<p<1 is an open problem in quasi-Banach space theory.
